meta.title: Late-handover liquidated damages (Housing Development Act statutory contracts)
meta.licence: Statutory terms and a court holding, recorded as facts with citations; no text of the instruments is reproduced.
caveats: Whether a materials shortage extends the developer's period (extension of time) was NOT verified. Do not state that a materials delay causes LAD.
LAD is owed per purchaser and only after each unit's own deadline.

facts.label: Liquidated damages for late vacant possession, as a fraction of purchase price per year, counted daily
facts.sourceName: Housing Development (Control and Licensing) Regulations 1989, Schedule H clause 25 (via National House Buyers Association)
facts.note: Same 10 percent in Schedule G. Counted 'from day to day'. PropertyGuru's worked example divides by 365.

facts.label: Day count used in worked examples
facts.sourceName: PropertyGuru, How much LAD can I claim

facts.label: Common facilities late: damages are 10 percent a year of this fraction of the purchase price
facts.sourceName: Housing Development Regulations 1989, Schedule H clause 27(2) (via NHBA)
facts.note: The last 20 percent of the purchase price.

facts.label: When the delivery period starts running
facts.value: date the purchaser paid the booking fee, not the date printed on the agreement
